description:
The Astronomical Observatory is located at the site of the former Royal Observatory. This historical venue hosts regular talks and viewings through modern and older telescopes, including the 1894 McClean telescope, located on a hydraulic floor.
Tours begin at the Visitor Center, where guests are introduced to the fascinating and rich history of astronomy in South Africa. This includes a visit to the main observatory building, one of Cape Town's oldest and most significant formal structures, and the reason behind the name of its surrounding suburb. Guests also have the chance to visit the library, browse an impressive collection of astronomical instruments, photographs, and exhibits that tell the story of South African astronomy through the ages.
Guests can also experience the magnificent McClean Telescope, undoubtedly the highlight of the night. This iconic instrument has played a crucial role in astronomical research and continues to inspire visitors with its impressive engineering and scientific legacy.
Weather permitting, the experience culminates in a stargazing session with both the historic McClean Telescope and SAAO's modern Dobsonian telescopes, offering breathtaking views of celestial objects, distant galaxies, and the wonders of our night sky.

First Thursdays is a monthly cultural experience centred around a walkable programme of art galleries, retail stores, restaurants and bars, taking place in both Cape Town and Johannesburg.
On the first Thursday of every month, dozens of art galleries stay open for extended hours, with additional cultural events showcasing the wealth of talent that the Mother City has to offer.
First Thursdays is more than just an evening of art. It is also a social occasion, with locals spilling out onto the streets, creating an electric vibe, drawing on the heady mix of local arts and culture and food and drink.
Visitors can start off in Long, Loop or Bree Street with a drink at any one of the popular bars, before browsing the galleries around the city centre – many of which provide visitors with refreshments – and finally settle in at one of the Mother City’s restaurants.
During First Thursdays, participating galleries showcase an eclectic mix of artwork, providing visitors with an inspiring visual feast. The renowned Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (MOCAA) in the Silo District is a must-visit destination. Housed in a repurposed grain silo, this contemporary art museum boasts an extensive collection that showcases the works of African artists. From thought-provoking installations to captivating paintings and sculptures, MOCAA offers a unique window into the African art world.
First Thursdays not only offers a visual and culinary feast but also a vibrant live music scene. As the evening unfolds, the city comes alive with captivating melodies and infectious rhythms. Throughout the participating venues of First Thursdays, visitors can enjoy a diverse range of musical performances, adding an extra layer of excitement to the event.
Beyond the art galleries and culinary experiences, First Thursdays Cape Town provides an opportunity to explore the city’s diverse neighbourhoods. Each district has its own unique character and atmosphere, offering a different cultural experience. The CBD (Central Business District) serves as the epicentre of First Thursdays, with many galleries and eateries concentrated in this area. The streets come alive with vibrant art installations, street performances, and enthusiastic crowds. The CBD’s narrow alleys and historic buildings add to the charm, creating a delightful ambience for exploration.
Various neighbourhoods offer their own take on First Thursdays. One example is Observatory, a bohemian enclave filled with quirky cafes, alternative music venues, and vintage stores. Its First Thursday - known as 'Late Night Thrift' - sees the neighbourhood buzzing with energy as thrift shops stay open late and live performances entertain passersby. Visitors can immerse themselves in the laid-back atmosphere, enjoy the vibrant creative spirit, and perhaps stumble upon an impromptu poetry reading or a live music jam session.

Norval Foundation presents a major survey of Brett Murray's sculpture, curated by Karel Nel, filling seven galleries with more than eighty works made over four decades. The show moves from his politically charged student work of the 1980s to the quieter, more personal pieces of recent years, and includes new works shown for the first time.
Murray is best known for sharp political satire, and this exhibition concentrates on his sculpture rather than his two-dimensional work. The animal world serves as a mirror for human behaviour, with primates, elephants, bulls, pigs and imagined hybrids rendered in polished bronze and marble. The postures of the animals raise questions about power, pride, fear and absurdity, balanced by a vein of empathy.
Murray draws on a wide range of references, from Walt Disney animation and East Asian vinyl toys to Brâncuși's polished forms and West African Baule figures. The scale of the pieces, including a monumental rabbit that towers over smaller ones, is possible because Norval's reinforced floors can carry works that other Cape Town museums cannot.

description:
Archery Adventures in the Howberry Hills of Plettenberg Bay teaches the art of archery to beginners and those with little experience in their Adventure Tour. The site can be found in the hills overlooking the Bitou River valley, with horses, farm animals and birdlife living in the property.
The Adventure Tour begins with an introduction and basic hands-on instructions lasting 20 to 30 minutes. The experienced instructor then takes guests for a hike through the indigenous forest to a nearby natural ravine where they’ll find a 3D Archery Trail. Tours can be booked in three different time slots, morning, midday and evening and breakfast, lunch and dinner are available on request. The tour includes equipment, targets and a certificate upon completion.
Tours last approximately two hours and are recommended for those 8 years and older. Archer’s Meals on the Deck are prepared by the team’s Austrian chef and are available to be pre-booked.
All targets used by Archery Adventures are hand-made and the organisation does not condone the shooting of live animals.
Price: R550pp
Venue address: Howberry Hills, Stofpad 18, Wittedrift, Plettenberg Bay

venue_raw: Montebello Design Centre, 31 Newlands Ave, Newlands, Cape Town
description:
Marimba Jam is a female-led NPO that invites beginners and music lovers to learn how to play the marimba in a fun lesson at the Montebello Design Centre. In between jam sessions, the guide and founder Kiara shares the history and journey of the instrument through Africa. Questions and interaction are always welcome.
The workshop begins with a short introduction and lesson about the different types of marimba and what sets them apart. Players then choose a style of the marimba to play between soprano, alto, tenor or bass and learn to play a popular or traditional song. Sessions include a 10-minute snack and water break and once players can play the song, a video of the individual or group is taken.
Marimba Jam provides more than one instructor for larger groups and can move the activity indoors in the event of rain. The location is child friendly as there are shaded playgrounds in the area.
Venue address: Montebello Design Centre, 31 Newlands Ave, Newlands, Cape Town
View map
Wheelchair accessibility: Unknown

The Cape Town Fynbos Experience creator Giselle Courney takes you on an ancient flavour ‘trail’ of aromatic infusions made from eleven of the 7000 species in the Fynbos biome.
The Cape Town Fynbos Experience® is a guided tasting of South Africa’s novel flavours that are unique to the southern tip of Africa.
Using infusion, unique botanical flavours are extracted with water, sugar, salt, oil, vinegar and alcohol to create herbal teas, cordials, culinary salts, vinaigrettes and digestives. The tasting room is filled with the fragrance of fresh fynbos plants, such as the cancer bush, rhino bush, and Buchu. At individual place settings guests find beautifully presented glass beakers with tea infusions, Petri dishes with fresh stalks of Spekboom and fynbos salts, and get to learn about the different botanical species and their properties.
Lunch is an experimental tapas accompanied by the South African Fynbos® range of seasonings and botanical infusions. The programme includes a scenic stroll on the Clairvaux estate, a haven for critically endangered Swartland renosterveld.
people.
Participants can take home the South African Fynbos® Flavour Wheel and a Fynbos herbarium.
Date: various dates - see website
Time: 10am to 2.30pm
Venue address: Clairvaux Estate, Robertson

Website: http://www.southafricanfynbos.com/

Eve Art Studio in Paarl is run by international artist Madeleine Eve, who teaches pottery and art classes. The workshops and classes are fun and relaxed and often coupled with wine or drinks. Visitors can come to her studio for a therapeutic experience of shaping and painting clay and socialising with other potters.
Eve Art Studio pottery classes are open to artists and those wanting to relax and try something new and teach how to work and create with all mediums of pottery. Guests should prepare to get their hands dirty and play around with different clays and paints in the studio. Adult painting classes are held on mornings and evenings, with kids painting classes also available to book during the day.
The studio is also available to book for private functions, bachelorettes, birthdays and corporate gatherings. All classes come with the required materials included.
Date: Mondays to Fridays
Time: 9am to 5pm
Venue address: 12C Louws, Southern Paarl, Paarl

Enjoy a slow Sunday morning with local creatives at the Bree Street Sunday Market, held alongside the car-free Bree Street Sundays, a pedestrian-friendly activation in Cape Town’s CBD that transforms Bree and Shortmarket Streets into a lively social hub. Gather at Clarke’s from 10am-3pm for great food, browsing, and networking. More information here.

The Vegan Goods Market brings together over 50 vendors offering delicious plant-based food, refreshing drinks, and cruelty-free home and body products. Add live music from local artists and a relaxed outdoor setting, and you’ve got the perfect Sunday outing for conscious food lovers. More information here.

The second annual Boeka on Bree kicks off at 6:30 pm, honouring the rich history of the Muslim community that has called the inner-city home since the late 1700s. Guests are invited to enjoy soup, dates, and water while taking part in a short prayer service and a historical talk. Bring a mat and something to share. Boeka on Bree is part of Bree St Sundays and is proudly hosted in collaboration with MSA Union, Radio 786, Cape Family Research Forum, AwqafSA, Salt River Heritage Society, Community Chess, Madina Institute, and Young Urbanists. Visit Young Urbanists Instagram page for more information.

venue_raw: Constitution Street, Harringtons Lounge, District Nightclub
description: Three venues. One street. Non-stop energy. Oh So 2000’s is taking over the streets for a Sunday daytime party. Think 2000s hip-hop and R&B anthems blasting from every corner — Usher, 50 Cent, Missy Elliott, Ashanti, Nelly, Destiny’s Child, Ja Rule, Beyoncé, Pharrell Williams vibes all day and night. Get your tickets via Quicket.

It’s the grand finale of Summer, and Kirstenbosch Summer Concerts has 5 epic shows featuring some of the country’s top acts. The line-up includes Derek Gripper and The Kyle Sheperd Trio (1 March), Matthew Mole (8th), Thandiswa Mazwai (15th), Will Linley and Ben Rodrigues (22nd), and The Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra and Rob Van Vuuren – Peter and the Wolf (29th). Get your tickets via Webtickets.

Step into the prize-winning Coniston Garden and experience a beautiful morning immersed in nature, while also discovering the fynbos restoration work taking place in Muizenberg Park. Begin with a gentle 30-minute walk through Muizenberg Park, followed by a one-hour guided tour of the Coniston Garden. The experience concludes with tea and delicious home bakes. The cost is R250 per person (100% of the proceeds go to the Fynbos Restoration Project). To book, WhatsApp John Venn on 067 382 4260 with your preferred date and time.

Spier Light Art returns to Spier from 6 March until 6 April 2026. Set among vineyards, the dam, river, and our historic buildings, the exhibition explores how light shapes memory, place, power, and possibility. Walk along winding pathways as artworks emerge from the night in playful, poetic, and provocative ways.

event_name: Kingdom of Ubuntu – The Musical in Concert
description: Experience a powerful Afro-epic musical journey that fuses live orchestra, African choir, dance, ritual, and storytelling. Set in a mythical African kingdom, this extraordinary concert celebrates unity across diverse clans, languages, and rhythms, while exploring timeless themes of love, betrayal, power, and leadership. When an exiled heir returns to claim the throne, the kingdom faces a pivotal choice: destruction or Ubuntu. The Kingdom of Ubuntu features South Africa’s most celebrated artists, including Mbuso Khoza, Ann Masina, Mbulelo Grootboom, Dizu Plaatjies, Bongiwe Nakani, and the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra. Book via Webtickets.

venue_raw: Streetscapes Vredehoek Garden, Rugley Rd corner Upper Buitenkant St, Vredehoek
description: Spend your Saturday morning exploring the Streetscapes Garden Market, a community hub for fresh produce, unique finds and local creativity. Enjoy fresh seasonal produce and organic compost, discover plants and garden treasures, delicious food and beverages, handmade crafts, home décor and thrift fashion, and plenty of unique, one-of-a-kind finds. Details here.

event_name: Kurt Schoonraad presents Funny Side Up
description: Everyone’s favourite funny man, Kurt Schoonraad, returns to the stage with his latest one-man show, Funny Side Up. In this laugh-out-loud performance, he takes audiences on a hilarious ride through the quirks and chaos of modern life, from everyday frustrations to finding the lighter side of a fast-changing world.Expect sharp wit, relatable stories, bold observations and plenty of classic Kurt charm. Book your tickets here.

Recognised as one of the world’s largest timed mass-participation cycling events, the Cape Town Cycle Tour continues to attract cyclists from across the globe to experience the beauty of the Cape on two wheels. The 109 km route takes riders around the Cape Peninsula, passing through Bakoven, Camps Bay, Clifton, and Sea Point.

Wine lovers, raise a glass to Harvest 2026 at the much-anticipated Tasting Under the Stars. Rather than a single central festival, this event sees each participating wine farms curate its own harvest-inspired event, forming part of a series of celebrations marking the end of harvest in the region.

Nora En Pure is bringing her iconic deep house grooves to the Mother City for an unforgettable night of music, sun, and waves. She’ll be joined by Monkey Safari, Chris Luno, Polar Inc, and Cornelius SA for a lineup that will keep you dancing till the stars come out. Grab your tickets and tables now via Howler.

For the very first time, Pretty Woman: The Musical is coming to South Africa! Based on the iconic 1990 film starring Julia Roberts and Richard Gere, this stage adaptation features music by Grammy Award-winner Bryan Adams and direction and choreography by Tony Award-winner Jerry Mitchell. A global smash hit; the show is a dazzling celebration of love, laughter, and nostalgia, guaranteed to captivate audiences of all ages. Don’t miss it, it’s running until 19 April 2026! Book tickets via Ticketmaster.

Cape Town Carnival turns sweet 16 this year, and it’s bigger and better than ever! Themed “Follow your heART”, the Carnival promises a spectacle of hand-crafted floats, intricate costumes, dance groups, and live performances from powerhouse artists like Zolani Mahola, Anslin Gysman, and DJ Ready D. Hundreds of performers, musicians, and community groups, including the ever-popular City of Cape Town Firefighters, will light up the route. More details here.

The Corona Sunsets Festival is back in the Mother City this month, from 12pm to 11pm, bringing a full day of music and vibes. Dance to an electrifying lineup featuring Purple Disco Machine, DJ Kent, LiquidDeep, Ndlovu Youth Choir, Sun-EL Musician, Zakes Bantwini, Mila-Rose, Msaki, Roz B2B Housewife, BlaqKongo, and Meek. An event you don’t want to miss! Book your tickets via Howler.

This March, rugby fans are in for a thrill as the DHL Stormers take to the field in two of the month’s most eagerly awaited clashes. On 22 March, they go head-to-head with the Dragons, followed by another epic showdown against Edinburgh on 28 March. Get your tickets

The Cape Town International Jazz Festival is an annual Cape Town event at the Cape Town International Convention Centre. The event brings together artists and jazz lovers from all over the world. The lineup is a mix of hot, up-and-coming musicians, local flavour, and big international names, including Jacob Collier, Sipho ‘Hotstix’ Mabuse, Nduduzo Makhathini, The Yussef Dayes Experience, and Salomão Soares. For more information, visit here.

The first-ever Montreux Jazz Festival in Franschhoek promises two unforgettable days of music, art, food, and wine. Inspired by the festival on Lake Geneva, this event celebrates music in all its forms. Performances will light up The Arches from lunchtime to midnight and Jazz Village from 3 pm to midnight on Friday and Saturday. On Sunday, the festival slows down with the Sunday Slowdown, featuring intimate music experiences scattered throughout the village along the scenic Montreux Mile. For the full lineup and ticket information, visit Montreux Jazz Festival’s website.

South Africa’s most premium daytime lifestyle event is back, and this time, PHOLA closes off the summer season with a 10/10 show you don’t want to miss. Expect world-class music in one of Cape Town’s most stunning settings. The line-up includes TKZee, Amaroto, Kentphonik, Kelvin Momo, Morda, Shakes & Les B2B Uncool MC. Get your tickets via Howler.

event_name: Karyn White and Ami Faku live at Kirstenbosch
description: Grammy-nominated American R&B singer Karyn White, the voice behind timeless hits ‘Superwoman’, ‘Romantic’, and ‘The Way You Love Me’, will delight fans with a one-night-only live performance. Set against the stunning backdrop of Table Mountain, this exclusive Cape Town concert promises an unforgettable evening of classic R&B, soul, and nostalgia as one of the genre’s most influential voices returns to the stage. Another superstar, Ami Faku, will open the show, captivating audiences with her soul-stirring blend of Afro-soul, R&B and gospel influences. Get tickets at Webtickets.

Learn more about Cape Town through a compelling storytelling dinner series hosted by LocalPlaces at the BlackBrick Gardens Rooftop in Cape Town. The series takes place during the first week of each month, offering an evening of delicious cuisine and storytelling that explores the history and development of Cape Town through the ages. Your ticket includes a welcome drink, a three-course menu, and the storytelling experience. The dinner will focus on the first era: Cape Town’s astonishing backstory, from ancient times to the Dutch period (1200–1795). Get your tickets here.

Reforest Fest is an environmental event that blends tree planting with live music, art, workshops, and sustainability activities. Hosted by Greenpop, the festival encourages visitors to help restore indigenous forests while enjoying a creative outdoor experience. On Saturday, the entire festival community comes together to plant 5,000 to 10,000 indigenous trees, a powerful collective effort that supports Greenpop’s year-round Uilenkraal Forest Restoration Project. This initiative aims to rejuvenate degraded forest patches, enhance biodiversity, and foster resilient ecosystems for the future. Get your tickets.
📍 Cape Town International Convention Centre

Get ready for The Ultimate Wine + Wildlife Sunset with Durbanville Wine Safari! Start your experience with a welcome drink, then enjoy a curated tasting of six wines showcasing Durbanville’s finest vineyards. Next, take a memorable Sunset Wildlife Reserve Drive to spot local wildlife. Plus, each ticket includes a Buy 1 Get 1 free Wine Safari Tour Voucher per person. Reserve your spot by emailing bookings@durbanvillewinesafari.com.

venue_raw: Twinell Rooftop, Cape Town City Centre
description: Cape Palooza is a rooftop lifestyle event featuring music, games, food stalls, and tattoo stations. The daytime festival celebrates youth culture in Cape Town with genres ranging from Afro-house to hip-hop and R&B. Get your tickets via Quicket.

venue_raw: The Company’s Garden – Entrance from Orange Street, opposite Mount Nelson Hotel, Cape Town
description: Get ready for a festival that will transform one of the city’s biggest landmarks into a glowing playground of light, art, and immersive digital installations. Local artists will collaborate to create displays that light up the night sky. As the landmark comes alive after dark, visitors can explore interactive exhibits, enjoy live performances, and sample food from local vendors. Get your tickets at Quicket.

Known as the “world’s most beautiful marathon,” the Totalsports Two Oceans Marathon draws thousands of runners from around the world. Participants run along scenic routes around the Cape Peninsula with stunning ocean and mountain views. More information here.

Soke celebrates African culture through music, fashion, food, and creative expression. Guests are encouraged to wear African-inspired attire while enjoying DJs and live entertainment performances. Get your tickets here.

R&B Only Lunch is a stylish daytime event designed for a 30+ crowd, hosted 27 floors above the city at Hotel Sky. With sweeping views of Table Mountain, the V&A Waterfront, and the surrounding skyline, guests can enjoy an afternoon immersed in timeless R&B classics in a chic sky-view venue. Expect sing-along hits from legendary artists such as Usher, Mariah Carey, Mary J. Blige, and Chris Brown, along with a special slow-jam session honouring the smooth ballads that defined a generation. Limited tickets are available. Get yours here.

This expo focuses on organic foods, natural beauty products, sustainable living, and wellness innovations. Visitors can explore exhibitors, attend workshops, and discover eco-friendly brands from across Africa and beyond. For more information on tickets, visit here.

event_name: Orms x Fujifilm x Vergelegen Photowalk
description: Photographers and creatives enjoy a scenic photowalk in collaboration with Fujifilm at one of the city’s most stunning wine farms. Combine your passion for photography, nature, and storytelling during a morning of fun and connection. The event takes place from 8:30am to 11am. Get your tickets here.

venue_raw: The District at 61c Harrington St, District Six, Cape Town
description: Back by popular demand, Bed By 10 offers ravers over 30 a chance to enjoy themselves without the after-effects of a late night out. Step back into the golden era of the 80s, 90s, and early 2000s as the resident DJ spins all the iconic club classics. Expect dazzling visuals, nostalgic anthems, and a truly retro atmosphere that will make you feel like it’s the good old days. The best part? You’ll be home and tucked into bed by 10. Grab your tickets via Howler and prepare for a night of retro fun.

event_name: The India Expo: Eastern Shopping Festival
description: The expo unites Indian culture, fashion, and lifestyle. Discover a wide variety of genuine products, including stunning clothing, jewellery, accessories, home décor, and more under one roof. For more information, visit here.

The 11th annual Agulhas Wine Triangle Harvest Festival introduces wine enthusiasts to the distinctive, cool-climate wines of Africa’s southernmost vineyards, as the region’s top producers gather for a single day to showcase their creations and share their stories. Participating wineries include Black Oystercatcher, Ghost Corner Wines, Land’s End, Lomond, Lost Boy Wines, Raka, Skipskop Wines, Sijnn, Strandveld Vineyards, The Berrio, The Drift Estate, The Giant Periwinkle, and Zoetendal Vineyards. Your ticket includes a branded wine glass per person, a tasting of 30-50 wines, entry, and live music. Get your tickets via Quicket.

event_name: Pick n Pay Wine & Food Festival
venue_raw: Claremont Cricket Club, Constantia Sports Complex, Constantia, Cape Town
description: Taste your way through some of South Africa’s finest wines and delicious cuisine at this annual festival. Wine tasters are provided with tasting tokens and a glass upon entry, and food stalls and live entertainment are available throughout the weekend. Tickets here.

Starting in April, Garden Court Victoria Junction will host a Sunday lunch buffet on the last Sunday of each month. Enjoy a generous selection of fresh salads, artisanal breads, hearty hot dishes such as lamb, chicken, and curry, and classic desserts. Priced at R375 per person, R185 per child under 12-years old, and children under 4 eat for free. For more information, email gcvictoriajunction.reservations@southernsun.com

This year’s edition of Ultra Cape Town features global acts like DJ Snake, Axwell, Afrojack, R3hab, Apashe, and Shimza at The Ostrich festival grounds. Expect immersive productions, light displays, and a high-energy dance music atmosphere that will keep you moving for hours. Get your tickets here.

Suidoosterfees is one of Cape Town’s most cherished cultural festivals, honouring the diverse range of South African art, music, theatre, and storytelling. Inspired by the Cape’s renowned south-easterly wind, the “Suidooster” programme features theatre performances, live music, comedy, dance, literature, and visual art, alongside talks, workshops, and events by both established and emerging artists. For more information, visit here.

Get ready to geek out at Comic Con Cape Town, the city’s biggest Pop Culture & Gaming Festival, returning for its 4th epic edition! This is your chance to dive headfirst into everything pop culture has to offer, from mind-blowing comics and merchandise to epic gaming experiences, immersive film activations, and some of the most inventive food around. Meet your favourite brands, connect with fellow fans, and celebrate your fandom like never before. Tickets via Howler.

Cape Town’s biggest pop culture and gaming festival spills into May with Comic Con Cape Town. Expect everything from comics, cosplay, and gaming to film activations, exclusive merchandise, and fan experiences. It’s a must for geeks, gamers, and pop culture lovers. For tickets, visit here.

venue_raw: Novalis Ubuntu Institute, Wynberg, Cape Town
description: Wander through a mix of thrift treasures, handmade crafts, holistic goods, and artisan deli stalls. Set in peaceful gardens, this community market comes alive with live music, food stalls, and plenty of hidden gems to discover. Entry is free.

Trail running enthusiasts and outdoor adventurers are invited to lace up for a cause at the Volunteer Wildfire Services Trail Challenge. This much-anticipated event combines adrenaline with breathtaking scenery to support the dedicated volunteer firefighters who protect the Western Cape’s natural landscapes. Starting from the Gardens Rugby Football Club, participants can choose between a 10 km or 20 km route, both of which traverse the trails of Table Mountain and Devil’s Peak. Get more information here.

event_name: Private Salon – Sar la Rouge – Digital Art & Charity event
description: A private home in Constantia opens its doors for a two-day immersive digital art experience that blends contemporary art, music, and community impact. At the centre is Franco-Togolese digital artist Sar La Rouge, known for bold, expressive portraits that explore how screens shape perception and reality. The opening evening (8 May) is an intimate sunset event featuring live music, curated canapés, drinks, and art throughout the house. The family day (9 May) offers a relaxed, interactive experience with workshops, kids’ activities, and full access to the exhibition. All proceeds support The Bridge Orphanage. Tickets available via Quicket.

Commissioned by The Market Theatre and The Baxter Theatre to mark the 50th anniversary of the 1976 Youth Uprisings, Rise ’76: The Story of June 16th is a powerful new South African work of historical fiction by Tiisetso Mashifane wa Noni, a two-time Fleur du Cap Award-winning playwright-director.

venue_raw: Hugo Lambrechts Music Centre, Cape Town
description: Candlelight Concerts’ special edition pays tribute to the legendary Brenda Fassie, celebrating her music through a powerful live performance bathed in candlelight. Audiences can expect a 60-minute concert featuring reimagined renditions of some of her most iconic songs, including Vuli Ndlela, Weekend Special, Too Late for Mama, Nomakanjani, and more. Tickets are available via Fever.

event_name: Nina Simone Tribute Dinner with Auriol Hays
description: Step into an evening with Auriol Hays as she channels the spirit and music of Nina Simone. Through song and storytelling, Hays brings Simone’s legacy to life, capturing the power and vulnerability behind the icon. For ticket prices and information, visit here.

event_name: Musgrave Gin Floral Workshop and High Tea
description: Hosted by Musgrave Gin in collaboration with uBlom, this exclusive event is elevated by a curated high tea by acclaimed chef Elsa van der Nest. Guests will create their own striking bouquet while enjoying refreshing pours of Musgrave Pink Gin or the non-alcoholic Musgrave Inspirit 0%. Afterwards, sample a high tea menu featuring buttery French sablés, finger sandwiches, a flourless chocolate cake with ganache, and a baked goat’s cheese quiche. For ticket prices, visit here.

event_name: Absa Run Your City Cape Town 10KM
description: This high-energy road race combines fitness with sightseeing as runners follow a scenic coastal route into the city centre. Even spectators can enjoy live entertainment and a vibrant race-day atmosphere. It’s a ‘proudly South African, proudly Cape Town’ must-experience mass-participation road-running event. Catch our Cape Town Tourism mobile team at the event and enjoy an immersive VR experience of the city. More information here.

venue_raw: Grand Arena, GrandWest Casino and Entertainment World
description: British synth-pop pioneers The Human League are set to deliver an electrifying night of pure 80s nostalgia, performing a string of timeless hits, including “Don’t You Want Me”, “Human”, “Together in Electric Dreams”, “Mirror Man” and “(Keep Feeling) Fascination.” Joining them as special guests are fellow UK synth-pop favourites Blancmange, whose cult classics “Living on the Ceiling”, “Blind Vision” and “Don’t Tell Me” have earned them a loyal global following. Tickets are on sale here.

Wine and food in one of the Cape’s most stunning locations? Yes, please! Begin the evening with a guided cellar tour led by winemaker Michael Langenhoven, offering insight into the winemaking process and varietals. Afterwards, tuck into a five-course menu created in collaboration with Executive Chef Terence Morris, with each dish thoughtfully matched to complement the wines and elevate every course. Tickets cost R1350. Email reception@montrochelle.virgin.com

A must for book lovers, this festival brings together leading authors, thinkers, and creatives for talks, debates, and intimate discussions, all set in Franschhoek. The Franschhoek Literary Festival, launched in 2007, takes place annually on the third weekend of May. Tickets from around R125 via the festival website.

Cape Town Opera presents a bold new staging of Carmen, Georges Bizet’s timeless opera. Set against a backdrop of jealousy and desire, the story follows the fiery, independent Carmen as she defies convention and captivates all who cross her path, ultimately setting tragedy in motion. Tickets are available via Webtickets.

One of Africa’s premier running events, the Cape Town Marathon draws elite athletes and casual runners from around the world. Renowned for its scenic yet fast route, the race is a highlight of the global marathon calendar. More information here.

venue_raw: Protea Hotel Stellenbosch and Conference Centre
description: Set in the heart of one of South Africa’s most striking wine regions, this curated experience brings together 17 top wine farms, great music, and plenty of space to relax and socialise. It makes for the perfect night of sipping and discovering your next favourite wine. Get your tickets via Quicket.

event_name: ACDC Duet Xchange 2026: The Art of the Duet
description: This two-night contemporary dance platform is presented by Anderson Carvalho Dance & Choreography. This artist-led platform is dedicated to duet-based collaboration, bringing together local and international artists to create new choreographic works rooted in dialogue and shared authorship. Guest choreographers and companies featured include New World Dance Theatre, Northern Dance Academy, and Janine Booysens. For more information and tickets, visit here.

The Jive Cape Town Funny Festival has been the Mother City’s ultimate cure for chilly winter evenings for more than two decades. Since its debut in 1997, the festival has consistently drawn sold-out crowds. This year’s edition promises a laugh-a-minute experience, featuring a stellar international and local line-up. Audiences can look forward to the mesmerising Italian shadow artist and illusionist Matteo Fraziano, the UK’s dynamic singing impersonator Mike Woodhams, the wildly inventive Spanish balloon artist Dani Airhead, and some of South Africa’s finest comedic talent, including Jason Goliath and Robby Collins. Get your tickets here.

The Good Life Show celebrates conscious living, food innovation, wellness, and sustainable lifestyle inspiration under one roof. Over three days, visitors can explore a curated mix of plant-based cuisine, health and wellness brands, eco-friendly products, and live cooking demonstrations from top chefs and industry experts. Tickets start at R150 and are available via Quicket.

Want to serve face, dance like it’s the early 2000s, and still be tucked up in bed by 10 (ish)? Bed By 10: LGBTQIA+ Edition is your throwback party for legends who love a big night out but love a good night’s sleep even more. Expect nonstop 80s–00s anthems, iconic drag performances, and live acts, DJ sets. Get your tickets via Howler.

Amapiano Fest is a major South African outdoor music festival and cultural celebration dedicated to the Amapiano genre, featuring top DJs, producers, and live performances. Book your tickets via Howler.

Garden Court Victoria Junction hosts a Sunday lunch buffet on the last Sunday of each month. Enjoy a generous selection of fresh salads, artisanal breads, hearty hot dishes such as lamb, chicken, and curry, and classic desserts. Priced at R375 per person, R185 per child under 12, and children under 4 eat for free. For more information, email gcvictoriajunction.reservations@southernsun.com

The Jive Cape Town Funny Festival has been the Mother City’s ultimate cure for chilly winter evenings for more than two decades. Since its debut in 1997, the festival has consistently drawn sold-out crowds. This year’s edition promises a laugh-a-minute experience, featuring a stellar line-up of international and local talent. Audiences can look forward to the mesmerising Italian shadow artist and illusionist Matteo Fraziano, the UK’s dynamic singing impersonator Mike Woodhams, the wildly inventive Spanish balloon artist Dani Airhead, and some of South Africa’s finest comedic talent, including Jason Goliath and Robby Collins. Get your tickets here.

Reggae legends UB40, featuring Ali Campbell, are heading to Cape Town this month. It’s the classic UB40 sound people love, with Ali’s distinctive vocals. You can expect all the favourites, including “Red Red Wine” and “Kingston Town,” plus many other hits. Get your tickets here.

This monthly wine-and-dine experience pairs some of the Cape’s finest wines with an intimate 5-course dinner. For June’s edition, the kitchen is reimagining comfort food in a whole new direction with the theme: “Same Name. Nothing Like You Remember.” Think familiar favourites reimagined with a modern twist. It’s a slow, relaxed evening where food and wine tell the story. Find out more here.

venue_raw: Theatre on the Bay, Camps Bay
description: Killer Queen, brought to you by the Luitingh Alexander Musical Theatre Academy, is a high-energy dance celebration of the legendary rock band Queen. Inspired by Freddie Mercury’s flamboyant stage presence and the band’s electrifying music, the production explores how four ambitious musicians rose to become one of the most iconic acts in music history. Packed with bold choreography, striking visuals, and Queen’s unmistakable spirit, Killer Queen delivers a thrilling night of dance and pure rock energy. Get your tickets via Webtickets.

event_name: Winter Symphonies at the City Hall
description: Cape Town’s Winter Symphonies series returns to the historic City Hall for four Thursday evenings in June, bringing orchestral music to one of the city’s most atmospheric heritage venues. It’s a warm, elegant winter tradition, with each concert featuring a carefully curated programme performed by leading conductors, soloists, and ensembles. Acts include conductor Arjan Tien with pianist Nikola Meeuwsen; conductor Arjan Tien with pianists Nina Schumann and Megan-Geoffrey Prins; conductor Bernhard Gueller with cellist Hayoung Choi; and conductor Bernhard Gueller with violinist Daniel Rowland. Tickets are available via Webtickets.

Set against the Overberg coastline, the Hermanus FynArts Festival transforms the seaside town of Hermanus into one of South Africa’s most exciting winter arts destinations. Throughout the festival, galleries, churches, wine estates, and public spaces across town come alive with visual art, live music, theatre, literature, film, sculpture, food, wine, and thought-provoking talks. One of the highlights this year is the closing concert by the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra on 14 June, which brings the festival to a spectacular finish. More information here.

Get ready for a night of magic! College of Magic presents a family show packed with laughs, surprises, and jaw-dropping illusions. See everyday objects float, vanish, twist, and transform right before your eyes… and sometimes even in your own hands. Book your tickets via Webtickets.

Start your morning by the sea with a good coffee in hand and even better company. This relaxed seaside walk brings together Cape Town’s dog-loving community for a chilled morning of connection, fresh ocean air, and plenty of happy, wagging tails. It’s super easygoing and social by the sea with your doggo in tow. Tickets are available on Quicket.

Mark World Oceans Day with a morning on the water. Bring your kayak, surfboard, SUP, canoe, or any other non-motorised craft and join this community paddle-out to celebrate ocean awareness, conservation, and connection. Please note that the event is weather-dependent. Find out more here.

Internationally acclaimed South African ventriloquist Conrad Koch brings his chaotic cast of characters to the stage, where they battle it out to become the ultimate puppet superstar. Of course, troublemaker Chester Missing has other plans, delivering brutally honest truths and throwing the competition into hilarious disarray. Expect plenty of laughs from fan-favourite puppets, including Gunter the German mosquito, Hilton the dramatic ostrich, DJ Hoodie, and Mr Dixon, the high school teacher. Get your tickets via Webtickets

event_name: Cape Town City Ballet: Orpheus in the Underworld
description: Loosely inspired by Jacques Offenbach’s comic operetta, this 1920s-inspired production brings the era’s glamour and chaos vividly to life. Think flapper girls, Mafia henchmen, Can-Can dancers, and even a penthouse swimming pool for the gods. With music specially arranged by Michael Tuffin, the ballet is a fun, fast-paced mix of love, mischief, and total mayhem. When Eurydice runs off with Pluto, Orpheus is secretly delighted, but once the meddling gods and the nightclub underworld get involved, things spiral into pure comedy and spectacle. Get your tickets here.

Fresh from his international tour, Don Vino returns to Cape Town for the latest edition of his high-energy live music experience, Saxy Vibes Vol. 8. Known for its fusion of soulful saxophone, this edition promises an elevated production, featuring appearances by some of Cape Town’s favourite musicians and a lineup of unexpected moments designed to keep the audience on their feet. Tickets available via Webtickets.

event_name: LGBT Market Day in the Winelands
description: The first LGBT Market Day brings Pride spirit to the heart of Paarl during International Pride Month, celebrating LGBT-owned businesses and community connection in one of the Cape Winelands’ most scenic settings. Experience locally made products, food stalls, live music, craft drinks, and seasonal favourites such as Glühwein. It’s part market, part social hangout. Entry is free. More information here.

Africa’s leading décor and design show is back, bringing together more than 230 of the continent’s most creative and innovative brands and companies under one roof. Whether you’re in the industry, planning a home refresh, or simply love beautiful spaces, it’s the ultimate place to explore the latest trends in interiors, décor, furniture, and lifestyle design. Find out more here.

Tulbagh’s much-loved Christmas in Winter Festival celebrates 25 years! The whole valley comes alive for a festive winter weekend packed with live music, markets, delicious local wine, and cosy fireside moments. Visitors can expect the famous Farmer’s Electric Light Parade, Glühwein stalls, live entertainment, family-friendly activities, and cosy fireside experiences throughout the valley. Grab your tickets via Webtickets and make a weekend of it.

venue_raw: M&M Music and Performing Arts College
description: Get ready for a Coachella-style music experience with ECHOFEST, brought to you by Kwena Music Academy. Packed with pop hits, R&B, and feel-good anthems, the show blends rich vocals with big-stage energy for a night all about great music and vibes. Arrive early for a meal before the performance. Tickets are available on Quicket.

Garden Court Victoria Junction hosts a Sunday lunch buffet on the last Sunday of each month. Enjoy a generous selection of fresh salads, artisanal bread, hearty hot dishes such as lamb, chicken, and curry, and classic desserts. Priced at R375 per person, R185 per child under 12, with children under 4 eating for free. For more information, email gcvictoriajunction.reservations@southernsun.com

One of South Africa’s most beloved winter events, the Knysna Oyster Festival combines sporting challenges, family-friendly activities, live entertainment, and, of course, plenty of fresh oysters. The festival attracts thousands of visitors each year and offers everything from cycling and running events to food markets and waterfront festivities. More information here.

event_name: The Old Cape Quarter Thrift Fest
description: Calling all vintage lovers, bargain hunters and sustainable fashion fans! At the monthly Old Cape Quarter Thrift Fest, enjoy a day of fashion, books, jewellery, handmade goods and unique finds. With dozens of vendors showcasing carefully curated thrifted pieces, it’s the perfect opportunity to refresh your wardrobe sustainably while supporting local small businesses. Entry is free. Find out more here.

Seafood lovers are in for a treat as the Sustainable Seafood Fest returns to the V&A Waterfront. Visitors can enjoy a fresh fish market featuring Abalobi, Fish4Africa, and Greenfish, as well as cooking demos, food and beverage vendors, entertainment and education zones, and live music. Entry is free. Learn more here.

Get ready for a night of pure nostalgia as R&B Fest arrives in Cape Town. Expect to sing and dance to hits from the ’90s and 2000s, with DJs spinning tracks from artists including Usher, TLC, Ashanti, Destiny’s Child, Sean Paul and Ne-Yo. The event promises to keep the party going well into the early hours. Get your tickets here.

Cape Town Gilbert & Sullivan Society brings this beloved comic opera to life, featuring pirates, romance, mistaken identities and plenty of laughs. With favourites such as I Am the Very Model of a Modern Major-General, Poor Wandering One and With Cat-Like Tread, this fresh and spirited Pirates promises laughter and musical brilliance for the whole family. Book now via Webtickets.

venue_raw: Corner Collingwood and Rawson Street, Observatory
description: Reconnect and recharge at the Southern Suburbs Holistic Festival. Featuring all things wellness, the festival, held on the first Sunday of every month, offers talks and workshops, wellness vendors with holistic products, and arts and crafts. For market info, email ssholisticfestival@gmail.com.

event_name: Disney On Ice: Mickey’s Search Party
description: Disney magic takes centre stage as Mickey Mouse and friends embark on an unforgettable adventure on ice. Featuring beloved characters from Frozen, Moana, Coco, Toy Story, and more, this spectacular production showcases dramatic skating, acrobatics, and out-of-this-world special effects. It’s one of Cape Town’s biggest family events of the winter season. Get your tickets here.

This cheeky, tap-dancing, jazz-handed love letter to theatre gleefully asks one important question: what happens when the Bard’s competition gets desperate enough to invent the musical? The answer, as it turns out, is chaos and plenty of rhyming couplets. In short: if you’ve ever loved musicals, Something Rotten! is here to roast them, toast them, and then serve them up with a flourish of jazz hands. Get your tickets via Webtickets.

Dress in blue, white and red to celebrate French heritage in the heart of the Cape Winelands. The annual festival offers wine tastings, gourmet food, live music and street entertainment. Don’t miss the popular Best Dressed competition, where festival-goers showcase their most stylish French-inspired looks. Get your tickets here.

Cape Town’s premier sustainable fashion showcase returns, featuring emerging designers, innovative collections and a celebration of local creativity. This year’s theme, “Trash to Trend,” challenges designers to transform recycled and waste materials into stunning fashion pieces. This movement was born in the heart of Khayelitsha and created to showcase talent and stories from townships and beyond. Book your tickets via Webtickets.

Boschendal’s much-loved annual Citrus Festival returns for two days of citrus picking, live music, good food, and genuine farm fun in the heart of the Winelands. A firm favourite on the Boschendal calendar, this year will feature a large covered seating area and bar, a weather-proof social space where you can relax, grab a drink, and enjoy multiple live bands performing throughout the weekend. Your ticket includes your citrus picking experience, a picking bucket, and 3kg of hand-picked citrus fruit. Get your ticket via Quicket.

The Cape Town Festival of Running is a premier event on South Africa’s road-running calendar, bringing together elite athletes, social runners, and fitness enthusiasts. The festival features a variety of race distances including 50km, 21.1km and 5km races. More details here.

Following her sold-out show last year, South African-born singer Salome is back, bringing This Is Me, a live experience celebrating women, resilience, and authenticity. The show will take you on a journey through Salome’s life, from her cultural heritage and personal struggles to her triumphs and self-discovery. Get your tickets here.

event_name: Soul Society Winter Edition: Christmas in July
description: Soul Society is turning up the heat this winter. Enjoy smooth R&B, Soul House, and soulful grooves from DJ Fabo, Will ST, Born2HouseMusic, Tino Nathan, and Summer Heynes. Whether you’re there to dance, socialise, or warm up this winter, this event is for you! Get your tickets via Quicket.

event_name: Time Out Market Winter Wine Series
description: The Time Out Market Winter Wine Series returns for another unforgettable season, bringing together exceptional wines, world-class chefs, and a community of wine lovers. In partnership with Time Out Market’s top chefs, enjoy a curated journey through food and wine pairings. Limited tickets are available here.

Award-winning singer-songwriter Simphiwe Dana joins the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra for a one-night-only symphonic performance that blends jazz, soul and African music. An experience you won’t want to miss! Secure your tickets here.
Drag-mime favourites Ramsay Davids and Martin Neethling return with a glamorous evening of comedy and musical nostalgia. Expect outrageous costumes, classic hits and plenty of laughs. Book your spot.

This exclusive international dining spectacle brings world-class chefs together under one roof to go head-to-head over a single legendary ingredient: tuna. On arrival, guests are welcomed with a spoon or fork and invited to taste tuna freshly sourced from the ocean. Then the competition begins. One by one, the chefs step into the arena, each unveiling their boldest, most inventive tuna-inspired creation. Your ticket includes unlimited access to the live tuna-carving experience, signature dishes from competing chefs, a bottle of wine, and live music throughout the evening. Get your tickets via Howler.

event_name: Taste of Terroir 2026: A Winter Red Wine Soirée
venue_raw: Loch Lynne Wine Estate, Durbanville Wine Valley
description: The Durbanville Wine Valley wraps up July in style with its signature winter celebration of cool-climate reds at Taste of Terroir. This curated evening brings together some of the valley’s top winemakers for a walk-around tasting experience showcasing the depth and character of the region’s award-winning wines. Your ticket includes unlimited red wine tastings from all Durbanville Wine Valley producers, live music, and three seasonal canapés from Kos Kouture. Get your tickets via Quicket.

The Carling Currie Cup returns to Cape Town, featuring one of South Africa’s fiercest rugby rivalries, as the DHL Stormers XXIII take on the Sharks. This Round 3 clash in the world’s oldest domestic rugby competition promises fast-paced action as the coastal rivals battle for early-season bragging rights. It’s a match you don’t want to miss. The DHL Stormers also face off against the All Blacks in the first of seven matches on the New Zealand rugby team’s seven-week tour of South Africa. More information is available here.

The 13th South African International Ballet Competition brings together some of the world’s most promising young ballet dancers. Competitors from South Africa and around the globe will perform in classical ballet and contemporary dance categories before an esteemed international judging panel. Enjoy dramatic solos, duets, trios and group performances. Find out more here.

This monthly wine-and-dine experience pairs some of the Cape’s finest wines with an intimate five-course dinner. For the August edition, savour award-winning wines from Lourensford Estate, perfectly matched to a chef-curated menu. Find out more here.
📅 6 to 29 August 2026 📍 33BREE, 33 Bree Street

As She Is is a powerful, non-profit photographic exhibition celebrating the beauty, strength and individuality of women living with disabilities. Marking the African debut of the internationally acclaimed Bold Beauty Project, the exhibition features striking portraits and personal stories of 17 women from the Western Cape, inviting visitors to challenge perceptions of beauty, identity and inclusion. Admission is free.

Based on the acclaimed novel Bottelnek Breek Bek by Dianne Du Toit Albertze, regarded as the first transnovel, the production will run for a limited time this month. The powerful drama follows Dora, a woman searching for belonging in a world marked by violence and hardship, as she discovers strength and sisterhood among the women around her. Combining humour, emotion and thought-provoking storytelling, the production promises a theatre experience like no other. Get your tickets here.

The Absolutely Fabulous Drag Show (ABFAB DRAG) returns to the stage to celebrate Cape Town’s vibrant drag scene. This year’s spectacular lineup features the incomparable Vida Fantabisher, Beaulah: Queens van die Kaap stars Manila von Teez and Kat Gilardi, Jayde Kay Johnson, Angel Lalamore, and Mitchell Darling. The production is dedicated to Soli Philander and Alfred Rietman. Learn more here.

Create, connect and reflect at this special workshop inspired by the practice of Cauleen Smith. Explore the mindful art of Ikebana flower arranging, enjoy a curated tea tasting, and raise a glass with celebratory bubbles. Find more information here.

event_name: Celebrate Her: An Evening of Wine, Dining, and Cinema
description: This Women’s Day, celebrate the incredible women in your life with an evening of great wine, delicious food, and a touch of movie magic at Pepperclub Hotel. Start with an exclusive wine tasting hosted by Carmen Stevens Wines, then settle in for dinner at COPA Restaurant. End the night with a private screening at the Odeon Cinema. Get your tickets.

Following last year’s sold-out celebration with Mi Casa, Feastival returns for a very special Women’s Day Edition. This unforgettable day celebrates the incredible women who inspire us, brought to life the Feast way, with delicious food, music, and lots of good vibes. Expect a food truck market, live bands, an epic DJ lineup, karaoke, a casino room, a secret dance floor, sip-and-paint experiences, a gaming room, cinema, spa experiences, wine and cocktail bars, and so much more! Get your tickets via Howler.

Step into the glamour of the Moulin Rouge at this dazzling disco-inspired party. Expect an unforgettable evening of house, disco and dance music, with epic ocean views. Dress to impress and celebrate Women’s Day weekend with a stellar line-up of DJs and live entertainment. Find out more here.

Celebrate Women’s Month by lacing up and joining thousands of runners and walkers at one of South Africa’s most iconic women’s road races. Whether you’re chasing a personal best or soaking up the vibes, the Totalsports Women’s Race welcomes participants of all fitness levels. After you’ve crossed the finish line, keep the celebrations going with live entertainment and exciting activations. More information here.

event_name: Champagne Breakfast at Lord Charles Hotel
description: Ladies, gather your besties and celebrate with like-minded women over a fabulous champagne breakfast at one of the city’s most beautiful hotels. This year’s theme, “Fabulous Fur,” invites you to channel timeless glamour in your favourite faux-fur, with prizes up for grabs for the best dressed. The celebration also features a curated fashion showcase by Luna and Me. Book your ticket here.

event_name: Amura Four-Hands Dinner: Ángel León × Alain Roux
venue_raw: Amura at the Mount Nelson Hotel
description: This August, Amura at Mount Nelson presents an extraordinary culinary experience as two of the world’s most celebrated chefs, Ángel León and Alain Roux, come together for an exclusive four-hands dining event. Bringing together six Michelin Stars, this limited series promises a journey of exceptional flavours, world-class technique, and innovative cuisine. From 13–15 August, Chef Alain Roux will lead the evenings alongside Chef Michael Nizzero and Chef Wandile Mabaso, presenting a six-course menu inspired by the finest local South African ingredients and his signature French culinary style. The experience culminates on 16 August with a landmark four-hands dinner featuring both Chef Alain Roux and Chef Ángel León. Each chef will present three signature courses, including their renowned lobster and kelp root creations, in a first-of-its-kind collaboration on the African continent. Book via Dineplan.

venue_raw: The Bay Hotel & Theatre on the Bay, Camps Bay
description: kykNET Silwerskerm Festival is one of South Africa’s biggest celebrations of Afrikaans and local cinema. There is something for every film lover, from must-see feature films and thought-provoking documentaries to short films, panel discussions, workshops, and industry masterclasses. The festival culminates in the prestigious Silwerskerm Awards, which celebrate the very best in local filmmaking. For more information, visit here.

Whisky lovers are in for a treat at The Only Whisky Show. Sample premium local and international whiskies, meet master distillers and brand ambassadors, discover limited-edition releases, and enjoy expertly curated tastings. More details here.

event_name: Vintage with Love’s The Big Sale
venue_raw:
Beluga Restaurant, Makers Landing
📅 27 to 30 August 2026 📍 Cape Town Cruise Terminal
description: This August, Vintage with Love presents a BIG week of sustainable fashion, featuring two unmissable events supporting literacy and education charities across South Africa. Discover designer brands, unique pre-loved treasures and incredible bargains. Every ticket purchased goes towards a good cause. Find out more here.

Experience the magic of Mandisi Dyantyis like never before as the award-winning trumpeter, composer, and vocalist joins forces with Real Wired Music and the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra for Mandisi Dyantyis: Symphonic Celebration. Mandisi reimagines his acclaimed songs for this one-night-only performance, brought to life by the soaring sound of a full symphony orchestra. Get your tickets at Webtickets.

Get ready for an evening of laughter as funnyman Yaaseen Barnes brings his brand-new stand-up comedy show, Just Jokes, to the stage. In a world that takes itself far too seriously, Yaaseen celebrates the value of silliness and reminds us that laughter is one of our greatest survival skills. Through sharp observations and playful storytelling, he explores why South Africa might be the funniest country on Earth. Get your tickets.

event_name: Time Out Market Winter Wine Series
venue_raw: Time Out Market Cape Town, V&A Waterfront
description: The Time Out Market Winter Wine Series brings together exceptional wines, world-class chefs, and a community of wine lovers. In partnership with Time Out Market’s top chefs, enjoy a curated journey of food and wine pairings. Limited tickets are available here.

One of rugby’s greatest rivalries returns to Cape Town as the Springboks take on the All Blacks. With the match officially sold out, the atmosphere at DHL Stadium is set to be electric as the four-time Rugby World Cup champions face their fiercest rivals in one of the most anticipated clashes in international rugby. More information here.

Garden Court Victoria Junction hosts a Sunday lunch buffet on the last Sunday of each month. Enjoy a generous selection of fresh salads, artisanal bread, hearty hot dishes such as lamb, chicken, and curry, and classic desserts. Priced at R375 per person and R185 per child under 12, with children under 4 eating for free. For more information, email gcvictoriajunction.reservations@southernsun.com

Yasmina Reza’s celebrated contemporary comedy ART arrives at the Baxter Flipside for a limited season, directed by acclaimed South African theatre-maker Marthinus Basson. Following the success of the award-winning Afrikaans production KUNS, the play follows three friends whose relationship is thrown into hilarious turmoil when Serge buys an expensive all-white painting, sparking a razor-sharp exploration of friendship, loyalty, identity and taste. Book your tickets via Webtickets or at the Baxter Theatre Centre Box Office.

The global musical phenomenon MAMMA MIA! is back in the Mother City! Transport yourself to a sun-drenched Greek island for this feel-good story of love, friendship and family, brought to life by ABBA’s biggest hits, including Dancing Queen, Mamma Mia and Super Trouper. Book your tickets here.

event_name: Artjamming Neon Slime and Kids Glow-in-the-Dark Workshops
description: Kids can get creative at Artjamming’s Neon Slime and Glow-in-the-Dark Workshops, with hands-on activities for plenty of messy fun. Make and customise neon slime, experiment with glow-in-the-dark creations, and let their imaginations run wild in a playful setting. More information here.

South African street food reigns supreme at the Capetown Kota Festival. Bringing together the best Kota experiences from across the Western Cape, the festival promises a full day of delicious flavours and entertainment. Tickets via Computicket.

The Time Dance Competition Gala celebrates the talent and versatility of Cape Town’s emerging dancers, featuring performances in ballet, hip-hop, tap, acro, and modern dance. The evening will conclude with a formal awards ceremony. Find out more here.

Get ready for an action-packed night of boxing as Fight Island brings a stacked fight card to Makers Landing. The evening features three championship bouts, including the WBC Silver International Super Bantamweight Championship, the WBF International Super Welterweight Championship and the WBF Africa Lightweight Championship, plus a series of international and local matchups. The event also doubles as a rugby watch party, with the Springboks vs All Blacks showdown screened live on the big screen. No under-16s. Get your tickets via Quicket.

event_name: A Night of Wine, Spirits & Intentional Connection
description: Spend an evening sipping and celebrating Cape Town’s Black-owned creative community at A Night of Wine, Spirits & Intentional Connection, hosted by Black Owned Cape Town. Meet local entrepreneurs and creatives while tasting wines from local winemakers, accompanied by a selection of light bites. The Black-owned wine bar will feature wines from Moedi Wines, Mukanya Wines and Kumusha Wines. Tickets are available via Quicket.

Venture beyond the expected with Nederburg’s immersive new sensory experience, Uncharted, launching as part of the acclaimed Dinner of Discovery series. This multisensory journey combines wine, sound, touch, scent and food to explore some of South Africa’s most evocative landscapes, all without leaving Nederburg’s historic home in Paarl. Find out more and book via Howler.

Spend an afternoon with the girls at this fun paint-and-sip experience, hosted by Bo-Kaap Deli and Studio Sals. Choose between a trinket tray and an incense holder, then get creative with your own paint kit while enjoying a drink and a sweet treat. Tickets are R210 per person, with limited spots available. Book via WhatsApp on 076 346 6207.

OUTsurance Gun Run brings a weekend of running, adventure and family fun. Choose your challenge, from the 21.1km Half Marathon and 10km Race to the adventurous 17km Trail Run, or keep things relaxed with the 5km Fun Run and 5km Pet Walk. Once you cross the finish line, the fun continues with food stalls and a play area for kids. Ready, set… Gun Run! Find out more here.

WOMAD (World of Music, Arts & Dance) Cape Town brings 10 days of music, arts and dance from around the world to venues across the city. The Cape Town programme showcases an exciting mix of international and local artists, traditional music, contemporary sounds, dance and storytelling. Highlights include the Korean K-Pop Culture Concert at Artscape, Indigenous Voices and Storytellers 2 at KAYA HQ, the Global Echoes Day Concert at UCT’s Baxter Concert Hall, and the Miriam Makeba Tribute Concert with the John Hassan Trio at Silvermist Wine Estate in Constantia.

Grammy-nominated singer Kenny Lattimore returns to Cape Town for a one-night-only concert. Known for his soulful vocals and timeless love songs, Lattimore will perform his greatest hits from his extensive catalogue, including For You, Never Too Busy and When I Said I Do. This marks his first major performance in Cape Town in more than a decade. Get your tickets via Webtickets.

Celebrate Heritage Day with an evening of South African wine, culture, fashion and live entertainment. Hosted by Chim’s Wine Tasting Events, the evening showcases a curated selection of wines from more than 10 Western Cape wine farms. The dress code is Heritage Chic. Get your tickets via Quicket.

Experience the thrill of a live circus and music as Zip Zap Circus joins forces with School of Rock for seven exciting performances. Full Tilt blends amazing acrobatics, aerial stunts, and live music, with performers and musicians feeding off each other in real time. The show supports Zip Zap Circus’s free youth programmes. Get your tickets via Webtickets.

venue_raw: Guga S’thebe Arts & Culture Centre, Langa
description: This immersive celebration brings together indigenous food, music, dance, and storytelling. Enjoy a welcome homemade beverage, explore an Indigenous Food Market and Harvest Table, and experience a traditional shisanyama. Traditional or culturally inspired attire is encouraged. Email cikizwam7@gmail.com for more information.

The Cape Town Spring Fair Celebration brings three days of good food, local finds and live music to the city. Spend the long weekend browsing more than 100 local artisan, food and beverage vendors, enjoying live music, and finding fun for the whole family. On 26 September, the Fog & Fire Heritage Saturday Community Market will help raise support for five local charities: SA Guide-Dogs, Animal Rescue Organisation, Honey’s Garden Medical Alert Dogs, Uturn and Living Roots. Entry is free. More info here.

event_name: Bafunny Bafunny: South African Festival of Comedy
description: South Africa’s best comedians unite as Bafunny Bafunny, the country’s national comedy team. The Cape Town leg showcases comedy heavyweights, including Trevor Noah and Eugene Khoza. The evening is packed with sharp observations and plenty of laughs. Find out more and get your tickets here.

The Cape Town City Ballet and the Norval Foundation present Velvet Feathers, a performance inspired by the timeless beauty of Swan Lake and other beloved classics. Your ticket includes a welcome glass of bubbly and canapés on arrival, a day pass to explore the Norval Foundation Museum and Sculpture Garden, photo moments with a professional photographer, and the performance. Get your tickets via Webtickets.

Cape Town’s nightlife scene unites for one unforgettable night at Red Bull Unlocked, celebrating the city’s best bars, clubs, speakeasies and music. This immersive, one-night-only experience invites you to explore different venues, discover new sounds and enjoy an exciting line-up of musical acts. Book your tickets here.

This vibrant eco-arts celebration brings whales, culture and community together, with live music, art, thought-provoking forums, delicious food, markets and plenty of family-friendly fun. Just 90 minutes from Cape Town, it’s an easy coastal escape packed with nature, creativity and memorable experiences. More information here.

Head to Paarl for the Boland Summer Festival, a three-day celebration packed with live entertainment, food, shopping and family fun. Browse more than 160 stalls, watch live performances, explore the Show N Shine car display, enjoy the funfair and rides, or relax in the Tasty Tea Garden. With activities for all ages, it’s a great way to kick off the summer season. Find out all you need to know here.

Ease into the weekend at Century City’s Summer Night Market. Tuck into street food, artisan crafts and live music. Open from 4pm to 9pm, it’s the perfect after-work outing for you and your family and friends. Convenient parking is available nearby, and the market is cashless. Find out more here.

Get behind the DHL Stormers this October as they face four big-name opponents at DHL Stadium: Hollywoodbets Sharks (10 October), Bristol Bears (17 October), Scarlets (24 October) and Ulster (31 October). Four home fixtures and lots of gees! Book your tickets via Ticketmaster.

Watch movies under the stars with The Galileo Open Air Cinema, returning for its 2026/27 season. Settle in at scenic venues with picnic treats, drinks, and entertainment, featuring a diverse lineup of classics and new releases for all to enjoy this summer. Here’s the full lineup.

Lace up for the Nelson Mandela Marathon, a celebration of his enduring legacy. Choose your challenge from the 42km, 21km, 10km, and 5km races, and join runners from near and far as you take on the course and experience Cape Town’s spirit. Marathon information can be found here.

Cape Town goes global as the world’s best blackball players descend on the city for the IBF World Championship. With athletes and delegations from 16 countries competing for the title, expect high-stakes matches set against the backdrop of Cape Town’s legendary hospitality. Find out more.

Get swept up in the kite action at the Cape Town International Kite Festival. Watch giant kites take to the sky, then stick around for family entertainment, kite-making workshops, food stalls and an amusement park. Now in its 32nd year, the festival brings colour and creativity to the outdoors while raising awareness of mental health. Get tickets via Quicket.

Mind Matters Summit takes over Cape Town with a city-wide programme of events, starting two weeks before the main event with Mental Mastery Week. The two-day Summit brings together ideas and practical tools for mental fitness, leadership, and mindset growth. Learn more here.

The ninth edition of the Western Cape’s biggest motor show features an action-packed lineup of high-octane thrills and entertainment. Expect drifting, spinning, off-road action, karting, stunts, more than 2 000 displays and interactive experiences, plus live music, food, a fun fair and passenger rides. Gates open at 10am, with free on-site parking available. Get your tickets via Webtickets.

event_name: Red Bull King of the Air
description: Cape Town’s famous summer winds set the stage for the return of Red Bull King of the Air, bringing the world’s best Big Air kitesurfers to Kite Beach for a spectacular display of skill. Watch riders launch sky-high against the backdrop of Table Mountain, with the competition held during a window when wind and swell conditions are at their best. The event is free to attend.

The inaugural Cape Town Coffee Show brings South Africa’s coffee community together for two days of coffee, food, and more. Taste coffees you’ve never tried, discover new beans and roasteries, meet the people behind them, and get up close to some of the best equipment and brewing gear. There’ll be tastings, cuppings, workshops, demonstrations, and expert insights from our education partner, the African School of Coffee. More information here.

Set against the slopes of Table Mountain, the Summer Sunset Concerts bring together great music, picnics, gardens and golden-hour views. It’s a highlight of the summer for music lovers. More information here.

Foodies, Taste of Cape Town is the place to be for a serious taste of the city’s culinary scene. Over two days, top restaurants, chefs and food makers serve more than 120 dishes, with live entertainment, chef demonstrations, tastings, pairings and plenty of hands-on foodie fun. Find out more here.
Streetopia is an annual event that brings communities and creatives together for a day of colour, creativity and good vibes. It’s free, and everyone’s welcome. Visit their website for more details.

Cape Town lights up for the festive season at the annual Festive Lights Switch-On. Head to the Grand Parade for a free live concert featuring some of the city’s biggest names before the lights go on. Entry is free.

Get ready for two days of fast-paced international rugby sevens as HSBC SVNS returns to Cape Town. Watch the world’s top men’s and women’s teams go head-to-head, with the Blitzboks facing the global competition on home soil. Expect big hits, quick tries, and plenty of off-field entertainment. Grab your tickets here.

Cape Town’s Young at Heart Festival (formerly the Cape Town Halaal Market) returns for three days of lifestyle, entertainment, and shopping. South Africa’s largest lifestyle exhibition brings together more than 350 exhibitors. Get more info here.

Unity On the Square returns to Greenmarket Square for its sixth edition, featuring some of South Africa’s favourite artists for an evening of live music. Gates open at 2 pm, with the show kicking off at 4pm and running until 11pm. Bring your sun hat, sunblock, and camping chair. Tickets via Quicket.
